title: Stuyvesant Casino weekends and the disastrous 1957 England tour with Condon
summary: Beside record dates he picks up weekend money, then tours England with the Condon band, where Condon's drinking and an insult to a society editor ruin the visit.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, of course, one of the things

- one of the many, many things we did out of Condon's
- of course - we did piles of record dates, as you know
and, uh, I was working Fridays and Saturdays - I went and
stopped by Bob Mall's place - you know, the place - over
on the Third Avenue, the Stuyvesant Casino, and I'd pick
up a couple of hundred bucks doing that over the weekend
on my way to work. So, it was really a great time and, then,
that's about the time that we all went to England - we
had a chance to go to England for a guy named Harold
Davison - the same spelling as mine, who was with a big
booker in England and we went over there and, of course,
---
Yeah - we had Bob Wilber and, uh,

But, anyway, we went there and
that was sort of a disaster scene; of course, everybody
was drinking a lot, especially Condon and, uh, I think
some of the people resented Condon's being so loaded
and, uh,---

He didn't perform the way they thought
he was going to.

Oh, yeah- that too. And, the first thing he did was get into trouble with the society editor in London paper with something he said; of course, if you know Eddie Condon, you don't pay any attention to those things, but this guy got insulted and he said - if this is Eddie Condon, go home and this such. And, that tour -- of course, my first European tour and, uh, the band was a big success but they hammered Condon all the way through it. And, you know, I suppose newspaper guys stick together and they just-- they said - well, say what you want about the band but don't mention Eddie Condon, you know. And, so, he got himself in a jam there because nobody ever wanted him back and none of the bookers would handle him, because of his conduct.
And, he never did go back - did he?
